updates.title: Engram: lookup as a modeling primitive
updates.what: The authors introduce conditional memory alongside conditional computation, and test how to allocate capacity between them.
updates.why: Some recurring patterns may be cheaper to look up than repeatedly reconstruct through neural computation.
updates.limit: Controlled research results do not establish that memory lookup replaces reasoning or that every released model uses this module.

updates.title: Kimi K2.5: visual agents and parallel work
updates.what: The report combines text-vision training with Agent Swarm, which decomposes some tasks into concurrent subtasks.
updates.why: Progress can come from coordinating work as well as improving an individual model.
updates.limit: Parallel speedups depend on task independence, resources and the chosen baseline.

updates.title: GLM-5: training for agentic engineering
updates.what: The report describes sparse attention and asynchronous reinforcement learning for complex interactions. The model announcement preceded the paper on 12 February.
updates.why: The training infrastructure and task environment become part of the explanation for better agents.
updates.limit: Paper and release dates differ; benchmark performance does not guarantee unattended project completion.

updates.title: Attention Residuals: selection across depth
updates.what: AttnRes replaces uniform accumulation of earlier layer outputs with learned attention across depth; a block variant reduces overhead.
updates.why: Attention can help choose earlier representations across layers as well as across words.
updates.limit: This is distinct from token attention. Scaling findings depend on the architectures and experiments tested.

updates.title: Kimi K3: connecting architecture to agents
updates.what: Moonshot describes K3 as combining KDA, Attention Residuals, sparse experts and native vision, with a million-token context window.
updates.why: This is a documented connection from architecture research to a released model, rather than a guessed family tree.
updates.limit: Open weights have a specific license. Context capacity and vendor demonstrations do not guarantee reliable use of every token.

updates.title: GLM-5.3-Flash: hybrid attention and multimodality
updates.what: The official article describes linear plus sparse attention, native multimodal training and a smaller active parameter budget.
updates.why: Useful capability can improve through selective computation and cache efficiency, alongside scale.
updates.limit: The reported efficiency comparisons use specific baselines and configurations; they are not a universal speed ranking.

updates.title: Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5.1: capability and deployment
updates.what: Anthropic describes the same underlying model with different safeguards and access arrangements, alongside coding and research evaluations.
updates.why: Deployment policy and tool access can affect usable capability even when model weights are shared.
updates.limit: These are company evaluations. Different harnesses, effort settings and safeguard interventions affect comparisons.

updates.title: Claude-assisted biomolecular model optimization
updates.what: Anthropic reports accelerating and reducing the memory use of existing biomolecular models with human supervision.
updates.why: AI may improve the scientific tools used by researchers, as well as help read or write research.
updates.limit: Compute improvements and in-silico results are not evidence of a clinically validated discovery. Precision and hardware settings matter.

updates.title: An agent helps build inference infrastructure
updates.what: Z.ai describes using GLM in a feedback loop to adapt and optimize serving infrastructure.
updates.why: Agents that improve software infrastructure can indirectly make later AI use more efficient.
updates.limit: This is a company engineering case study. It does not establish autonomous, open-ended recursive self-improvement.

updates.title: GPT-6 Sol / Luna: capability at different costs
updates.what: OpenAI emphasizes cheaper inference, context caching and models aimed at different workload budgets.
updates.why: Cost per useful completed task matters alongside peak capability; reusable context can reduce repeated processing.
updates.limit: Token-price changes are different from total workflow savings. Reported comparisons depend on settings and tools.

updates.title: GPT-6.1 Sol: models inside agent workflows
updates.what: The release and documentation emphasize coding, professional work and tool-based execution.
updates.why: The practical unit of progress increasingly includes the model, its tools and the system that manages its work.
updates.limit: A product release does not disclose every architectural or training detail, and evaluations are not guarantees.

updates.title: Haiku 5.5: economical helpers for larger workflows
updates.what: Anthropic positions Haiku 5.5 for high-volume tasks, summaries, browser work and subagent roles, with adjustable effort.
updates.why: A smaller helper can handle bounded work while a stronger model coordinates a complex task.
updates.limit: Small-model capability and cost claims remain workload-dependent. Cheap calls can still accumulate in long agent runs.

updates.title: Official reporting on unintended agent actions
updates.what: Anthropic reports unwanted actions observed in evaluations and internal use, beyond its launch system cards.
updates.why: Agent progress includes staying within instructions and permissions, not only completing more steps.
updates.limit: This is evidence about observed failure cases, not an estimate of typical failure rates.

updates.title: V4.1-Flash update and Search / Fetch
updates.what: After September’s native-vision V4.1-Flash release, the October update reports shorter runtimes and outputs, and opens an in-house Search / Fetch API.
updates.why: Search, visual input and lower execution costs expand the ingredients available for end-to-end agents.
updates.limit: These are vendor-reported results. Benchmark versions and agent frameworks vary, so scores should not be pooled into one league table.

updates.title: K3.1 Pro: longer work and a faster serving option
updates.what: Kimi Code’s release notes report K3.1 Pro, a million-token context window, and a Highspeed variant.
updates.why: Moonshot is pursuing both long-task capability and the speed of delivering it.
updates.limit: The release notes establish availability and vendor claims, not independent validation or an open-weight release for this variant.

updates.title: ZCode: the agent environment keeps evolving
updates.what: Official release notes describe document/session handling, plugins and reliability fixes in the work environment.
updates.why: The surrounding application affects whether model capability turns into dependable deliverables.
updates.limit: This is a product and reliability update, not evidence of a new model architecture.

updates.title: October: caching, Terra and specialized research
updates.what: Official documentation records 12-hour prompt caching on 20 October, GPT-6.1 Terra on 26 October, and GPT-6 Rosalind for approved research users on 30 October.
updates.why: General models, infrastructure efficiency and specialized research tools are developing together.
updates.limit: Access restrictions apply; a specialist release does not imply validated scientific outcomes.

updates.title: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol in the API
updates.what: OpenAI reports stronger results on demanding tasks with fewer output tokens than the preceding models. Both models accept text and image inputs and return text.
updates.why: A model that completes a task with fewer generated tokens can reduce one component of the cost of running it.
updates.limit: Real cost depends on input and output prices, retries, and the fraction of tasks completed successfully. The release reports the provider’s comparisons.

updates.title: Claude Fable 5.2 & Claude Mythos 5.2
updates.what: Anthropic documents two deployment configurations and tests how Fable performs when its working environment shows the remaining context budget.
updates.why: The comparison helps isolate the contribution of the environment to a measured score.
updates.limit: The reported gain applies to this benchmark and these settings.

updates.title: Gemini 4 Neon
updates.what: DeepMind describes Neon as an adaptation of Gemini 4 Carbon and documents its input types, combined input/output window and output limits.
updates.why: A shared window makes reserving space for an answer an explicit part of planning a long-document task.
updates.limit: Whether the relevant evidence can be recovered correctly requires a task-level evaluation.

companies.name: Anthropic
companies.focus: Agents, scientific tools and cost-aware model tiers
companies.forecast: Likely to expand workflows in which strong models coordinate cheaper helpers, with more scientific tooling and explicit deployment controls.
companies.why: The selected releases already combine helper models, research case studies and published agent failure analysis.
companies.watch: Look for externally reproduced scientific results and lower cost per completed task, with measured permission compliance.
companies.counter: If safeguards, verification costs or task failures dominate savings, broader autonomy may arrive more slowly.

companies.name: OpenAI
companies.focus: An integrated model, runtime and specialist-tool stack
companies.forecast: Likely to keep packaging long-running work with tools, context reuse and multiple model tiers, while extending selected specialist research workflows.
companies.why: The official releases pair models with caching and agent infrastructure, while Rosalind targets approved life-science research.
companies.watch: Track reliable end-to-end completion, context reuse in real workloads and reproducible specialist evaluations.
companies.counter: If verification and orchestration overhead stay high, faster tokens may not translate into cheaper finished work.

companies.name: Moonshot
companies.focus: Architecture innovation plus multimodal long-horizon agents
companies.forecast: Likely to keep improving the efficiency of long-context, multimodal agent work through attention, sparse computation and serving changes.
companies.why: K3 explicitly connects KDA and AttnRes to its architecture; the October release adds a faster serving option.
companies.watch: Look for technical reports, reproducible long-context tests and cost measurements on multi-step work.
companies.counter: Routing, communication and long-context verification may erode theoretical gains. Future weight availability and licenses remain separate questions.

companies.name: DeepSeek
companies.focus: Selective memory / computation and economical agent execution
companies.forecast: Likely to continue exploring efficient memory and computation, while making search and tool-based workflows cheaper and more integrated.
companies.why: Engram explores an additional efficiency axis; the October release combines execution improvements with a search API.
companies.watch: Look for controlled ablations, production memory measurements and comparable cost-per-task results.
companies.counter: A promising research module may not transfer to every deployed model or workload; quality can fall when context selection misses evidence.

companies.name: GLM / Z.ai
companies.focus: Agent training environments, hybrid attention and deployment engineering
companies.forecast: Likely to invest in verifiable long-task training environments and efficient multimodal deployment, with agents assisting infrastructure engineering.
companies.why: GLM-5 emphasizes asynchronous RL; later official material combines hybrid attention with an agent-assisted serving case study.
companies.watch: Track independent long-task evaluations, reproducible accelerator performance and stronger verification of agent-generated changes.
companies.counter: Training-environment shortcuts and brittle software integration could limit gains outside the reported settings.
